- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 1–3%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop; adjust forecast downward by 1–4% to reflect mean reversion.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mixed; reduce first 5–7 forecast values by 1–3% to align with historical mean reversion.
- When sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “0.67” patterns, model tends to ignore sentiment and forecast based on recent price momentum — override with sentiment-weighted adjustment (e.g., +0.5–1.0% for positive sentiment, -0.5% for negative).
- For 30-day forecasts, if first 5–7 days show high volatility or sentiment swings, reduce forecast variance by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
